title: 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976
lead: The ==high-water mark of parliamentary sovereignty over constitutional supremacy== in India's history — and its subsequent partial reversal is equally central to understanding how the ==Basic Structure doctrine== was consolidated. The most consequential and most controversial amendment India has seen.

items.title: Preamble & Ideology
bullets: Inserted ==‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and ‘Integrity’==, changing ‘Sovereign Democratic Republic’ to ==‘Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic’==

items.title: Fundamental Duties
bullets: New ==Part IV-A (Art 51A)== prescribing ==ten Fundamental Duties== — respect for the Constitution, Flag and Anthem, environmental protection, scientific temper
Inspired by the erstwhile ==USSR's constitutional model==

items.title: DPSPs vs Fundamental Rights
bullets: Amended ==Art 31C== to give ==all of Part IV== (not just Arts 39(b)/(c)) primacy over ==Arts 14, 19 and 31==, and ==barred judicial review== of DPSP-implementing laws
Added ==Art 39A== (equal justice, free legal aid) and ==Art 43A== (workers' participation in management)

items.title: Curtailment of Judicial Review
bullets: ==Art 32A==: barred the SC from examining ==state law validity== in Art 32 writs
==Art 131A==: gave the SC ==exclusive jurisdiction== over Central law validity, excluding HCs
==Art 144A==: required a minimum bench and ==two-thirds majority== to strike down a Central law
==Art 226A==: barred HCs from examining ==Central law validity==; ==Art 228A==: similar restriction on state laws
Diluted ==Arts 226/227== — narrowed writ grounds and curtailed HC superintendence

items.title: Amending Power
bullets: ==Art 368(4)==: no constitutional amendment could be ==questioned in any court on any ground==
==Art 368(5)==: ==no limitation whatsoever== on Parliament's constituent power — a direct attempt to ==nullify Kesavananda's Basic Structure doctrine==

items.title: Centre–State, Elections & Administration
bullets: ==Art 257A==: Union could deploy ==central armed forces without state consent==
Extended emergency powers and central legislative competence — ==tilting the federal balance==
==Lok Sabha and Assembly terms extended from 5 to 6 years==; the 1971-elected LS extended by a year, ==postponing the 1976 general election==
Moved ==Education, Forests, Weights and Measures, Protection of Wild Animals and Birds== from State to ==Concurrent List==
Enabled an ==All India Judicial Service==; added ==Arts 323A and 323B== for Administrative Tribunals (==this survived==, operationalised via the 1985 Act)
Made the President ==explicitly bound by CoM advice (Art 74(1))== — retained even after 1978

head: Dimension
Impact
rows: Sharply tilted power toward the executive by ==insulating amendments and DPSP-based laws from judicial review==.
==Centralised== legislative and administrative power by expanding the Concurrent List.
Diminished the primacy of ==Arts 14, 19 and 31== relative to Directive Principles.
Introduced, for the first time, a ==codified sense of civic obligation== — shifting discourse to include duties alongside rights.
==Undermined electoral accountability== by postponing elections and extending tenure — among the most authoritarian features of the Emergency era.
Provoked the strongest judicial push-back in independent India's history ([[Minerva Mills, 1980]]), ==cementing the Basic Structure doctrine== as an entrenched limit on Parliament's amending power.

head: Original 42nd CA change
Reversed by
Nature of reversal
rows: ==Struck down==; judicial review over amendments restored as a facet of Basic Structure.
Struck down; amending power ==limited by Basic Structure== (Kesavananda upheld).
==Art 31C== — all DPSPs given primacy over Arts 14, 19, 31
Extension to ‘all DPSPs’ struck down; only the ==pre-42nd position (Arts 39(b)/(c))== survived, and remains reviewable.
Art 32A — SC barred on state laws
Omitted; ==SC's Art 32 writ jurisdiction fully restored==.
Art 131A — exclusive SC jurisdiction on Central laws
Art 226A — HCs barred on Central laws
Art 228A — restriction on HCs re state laws
Suspension of Arts 20 & 21 in Emergency (per [[ADM Jabalpur]])
==Expressly barred== — Arts 20 and 21 can ==never be suspended==, even in a National Emergency.
Replaced with the narrower, more objective ground of ==‘armed rebellion’==.
Art 31C limits on reviewing DPSP laws
Minerva Mills (1980); reaffirmed in [[Waman Rao (1981)]] & [[I.R. Coelho (2007)]]
Judicial review restored; ==‘prospective overruling’== applied to Ninth Schedule insertions.
